title: Chapter 2942 - 173: Want You Dead_2
content:
Chapter 2942: Chapter 173: Want You Dead_2

The Pavilion Elder couldn’t help but rub his fingers together.

But in the end, he managed to restrain himself with great effort.

Peering into someone’s foundational life roots is a major taboo in Tao Cultivation.

Of course, for someone of the Pavilion Elder’s caliber, this doesn’t really count as a "major taboo".

He has lived too long, his cultivation is too high, his divine sense too strong, his experience too deep, he sees through heavenly secrets, and his skills cover cause and effect.

Often, when someone walks past him, just a glance allows him to discern their "Dao" clearly.

Their disposition, foundational strength, heritage, the path of cultivation, the route they have chosen... all clear and transparent.

But Mo Hua is not an ordinary person.

His Taoist Heart is pure, he treats others sincerely, akin to uncut jade. But when studied deeply, he seems like an abyss, with vast cause and effect and deep heavenly secrets...

The Pavilion Elder thought about it and decided to let it go after all.

"I’m retired, I’m retired, I’m retired..."

The Pavilion Elder whispered it three times to dispel the curiosity and obsession in his heart.

But his heart was still restless and hard to calm.

The Pavilion Elder sat by the pond, his gaze deep, watching the rippling water’s surface, watching the fish swimming in the water, and slowly reviewing the cause and effect behind it all.

Yet the more he reviewed, the clearer his heart became...

The situation at the Qian Learning State Boundary was initially a "deadlock".

Originally, more people would have died, countless forces implicated, many aristocratic families and sects would have been wiped out.

Most people have no concept of the word "disaster".

Nor do they know what the word "disaster" truly means.

They don’t know the terror of the Evil God.

They don’t know that the Qian Learning State Boundary was once truly precarious.

They don’t know their lives and deaths were once separated by a mere thread.

And now, although the Qian Learning State Boundary seems to have "calmed", aristocratic families continue vying for power, sects continue competing for benefits, under the guise of fame and profit, everything appears to be "flourishing".

People’s memories of that great catastrophe have started to fade.

Forget the pain once the scar heals; it’s human nature.

But as the manipulator, the Pavilion Elder understands better than anyone.

If no one broke the deadlock, and no one in the shadows took responsibility and drove these developments, if no one ventured to risk and destroy the Great Wilderness Evil God’s plans, then years ago the "Qian Learning Catastrophe" would have already been the end of the Qian Learning State Boundary.

But matters of the Divine Way are profoundly deep and extremely dangerous.

Even as the Pavilion Elder, he initially didn’t have a good "piece" to break this deadlock, to find ways to minimize fatalities among the many state boundary sentient beings in the Evil God’s disaster.

Fortunately, there was Mo Hua.

But Mo Hua initially just wanted to be a "lazy fish", not wanting to be implicated.

So the Pavilion Elder didn’t hesitate at any cost, even risking great taboo and offenses against the Taoist Court, using the "Yin Yang Rebirth Formation" as bait to lure out Mo Hua, the "little Golden Dragon Fish", to stir the waters and break the deadlock at Qian Learning, allowing the Qian Learning State Boundary to continue.

This undertaking was very dangerous and risky.

But concerning the overarching situation, as Pavilion Elder, he naturally did so unswervingly.

But the Yin Yang Rebirth Formation has far-reaching cause and effect lines, and if it truly gets investigated, he, as Pavilion Elder, truly wouldn’t be able to escape responsibility.

Thus, he directly "resigned" and made his escape.

Of course, doing so isn’t just about the "Golden Dragon Fish".

Over these many years as Pavilion Elder, peering into heavenly secrets, strategizing, he’s carried too many grand causes and effects.

There’s an even more terrifying cause and effect lying in wait for him.

To seek complete life from the Heavenly Dao, and to withdraw from the game to view the chess match as an observer, "braving the currents and retreating" was the best choice.

But now, as the Pavilion Elder sorted out the cause and effect lines, he realized a significant problem.

This significant problem lies with this "Golden Dragon Fish".

In the Qian Learning State Boundary, this Golden Dragon Fish took the "bait" he threw, followed his line, and broke the Qian Learning deadlock.

This was within his expectations.

Furthermore, this "bait" was too large, too solid, too ancient; surely, this little Golden Dragon Fish can’t swallow it.

As long as the "bait" remains, then the line attached to the "bait" remains as well.

This is also the Pavilion Elder’s precaution, the hidden cause and effect "dark line" he left behind.

If the old Taoist Court fuss figures eventually come to "settle accounts" with him, he can follow the line and retrieve the "bait".

But now, things are not right...

This Golden Dragon Fish has swum out of the Qian Learning State Boundary, gone far into the Great Wilderness, unknown what it did, suddenly it "ate" the bait and swallowed it, preparing to digest it.

This bait became the key to shaping this "Golden Dragon Fish’s" Life Formation.

In other words, his actions are actually helping this Golden Dragon Fish to "Core Formation" Dragon Transformation.

Now this cause and effect... has truly pierced the heavens, grown immensely large.

The Pavilion Elder is more and more alarmed as he ponders this cause and effect.

To the point that he feels like a fisherman on the shore, only to have his bait and hook pulled by the fish, falling headlong into the water.

Moreover, it’s indisputable.

After all, the Yin Yang Rebirth Formation was "sent" out by him, the Pavilion Elder.

Now this Yin Yang Rebirth Formation has been fused by that kid as a Life Formation...

Such an outrageous affair...

As this "deeply scheming" Pavilion Elder, if he claims he truly didn’t do it intentionally... he doubts anyone would believe him.

Anyway, convincing the suspicious old Taoist Court figures might be a bit challenging...

The Pavilion Elder doesn’t quite believe himself.

He doesn’t believe this ancient "bait" could actually be eaten by a fish.
